'''Patrick Edward Dorey''' is a British mathematical physicist. He is a Professor in the Department of Mathematical Sciences at [[Durham University]].<ref name="hp">{{cite web |title=Professor Patrick Dorey |url=https://www.durham.ac.uk/staff/p-e-dorey/ |publisher=Durham University |access-date=8 July 2025 |language=en-gb}}</ref>

== Education ==
Dorey completed his PhD in 1990 at [[Durham University]], where he was supervised by [[Ed Corrigan]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Dorey |first=Patrick Edward |title=The exact S-matrices of affine Toda field theories |publisher=Durham University |year=1990 |url=https://etheses.dur.ac.uk/6473/1/6473_3773.PDF?UkUDh:CyT}}</ref>

== Career ==
Dorey returned to Durham in 1993 after working as a [[postdoc]] at [[Institute of Theoretical Physics, Saclay|Saclay]] and [[CERN]]. His main research interest is conformal and integrable field theories.<ref name=hp /> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] in 2000.<ref name=hp />

He has also served as a visiting lecturer at the [[African Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] (AIMS) in [[Cape Town]], South Africa, where he remains an associate faculty member.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Associate Faculty of AIMS South Africa |url=https://aims.ac.za/associate-faculty-of-aims-south-africa/ |website=AIMS South Africa |access-date=8 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=African centres hope to produce top mathematicians |url=https://www.scidev.net/global/news/african-centres-hope-to-produce-top-mathematicians-1/ |website=SciDev.net |access-date=8 July 2025}}</ref>
